descript.abstract: The Digital Elevation Model dataset consists of tiled LiDAR DEM Images. Each file contains a Raster Image of the Digital Elevation Model. The Geographical Extent of this dataset extends to the entirety of the FL_MiamiDade_D23 boundary in the State Plane Florida approximately 1169 square miles of the AOIs.
descript.purpose: The USGS contracted Digital Aerial Solutions, LLC to obtain professional services related to the planning, acquisition and development of Light Detection and Ranging (Lidar) data and derivative products. The task order is for a QL1 Lidar survey to be collected over Miami Dadecounty. The deliverable products would be used by the USGS to support State of Florida and the 3DEP mission.
descript.supplinf: All Lidar data and associated products were acquired, calibrated, and used in the creation of Lidar derived products by Digital Aerial Solutions, LLC to meet U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) - National Geospatial Program (NGP) Lidar Base Specification v2022 rev. A Raster File Type = GeoTIFF Bit Depth/Pixel Type = 32-bit float Raster Cell Size = 2.0 feet Interpolation or Resampling Technique = Bilinear Interpolation Required Vertical Accuracy = 19.6 cm NVA

dataqual.logic: Aerial LiDAR data covers the entire 1169 square miles Area of Interest intended for this project.All LiDAR Point Cloud tiles show no edge artifacts or mismatches from tile to tile. Void areas (i.e., areas outside the project boundary but within the tiling scheme) are coded using a unique “NODATA” value. This value is identified in the appropriate location within the file header. Data cover the entire area specified for this project.
dataqual.complete: The RAW LAS data files included all data points collected. No points have been removed or excluded. A visual qualitative assessment was performed to ensure data completeness. No void areas or missing data exist. The RAW point cloud is of good quality and data passes Fundamental Vertical Accuracy specifications. Void areas (i.e., areas outside the project boundary but within the tiling scheme) are coded using a unique “NODATA” value. This value is identified in the appropriate location within the file header.

vertacc.vertaccr: "This data set was produced to meet ASPRS Positional Accuracy Standard for Digital Geospatial Data (2014) for a 10-cm RMSEz Vertical Accuracy Class."

procstep.procdesc: Bare-Earth DEM Creation: Bare-Earth Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) were derived using the bare-earth (ground) LiDAR points, all DEMs were created with a grid spacing of 2.0 feet. The DEMs were cut to tiles of 5,000 feet X 5,000 feet index.
